en: The Sūtra of the *Aṣṭottaraśata-dhāraṇī-ārya-lokeśvara*. [Biography of] the Grand Master of the Court,
Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Duke of Susuo with a fief of three thousand households,
recipient of the purple robe, posthumously titled Minister of Works and conferred the posthumous name Dajian (Great Mirror).
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Bhagavat was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, the Garden of Anāthapiṇḍada.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of the Great Xingshan Temple, who possesses Great and Vast Wisdom, by imperial decree.
Together with an immeasurable assembly of bodhisattvas,
at that time the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara rose from his seat amidst the great multitude.
Having adjusted his robes and bared his right shoulder,
he knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms in reverence,
prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Bhagavān, I now wish to speak of that which can accomplish all the supreme dharmas of the three periods of time.
I only pray that the Bhagavān, out of compassion, will grant me permission.
At that time, the Bhagavān praised him, saying: "Excellent, excellent, Mahāsattva!"
For the sake of the great benefit of all sentient beings,
you wish to proclaim such a treasury of secret Dharma;
I now grant you permission to explain it in detail as you see fit.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara spoke this mantra:
Oṃ aruke svāhā. When the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara had finished speaking this mantra...
He then addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, this mantra is the heart-mantra of the entire Lotus Family.
I shall now proclaim the rules for its siddhi.
If, every morning at dawn, one performs [the rite] before my image..."
Construct a maṇḍala and scatter various kinds of flowers;
recite [the mantra] eight thousand times.
Furthermore, without speaking to anyone else, recite it some more.
Gradually, one will develop a powerful memory;
if one follows this method for six full months,
one will become greatly intelligent.
One should receive and never forget all that is heard.
Having performed a pure ablution,
one should construct three circular altars before the Buddha.
The Buddha is first, the Dharma second, and the Sangha third.
Offer flowers and incense to each according to the Dharma;
having offered them by holding an incense burner and burning incense with one's own hands.
If one recites this eight thousand times,
all grave offenses— including those leading to rebirth in hell, the four grave offenses, and the five heinous crimes— will be extinguished without exception;
of this there is no doubt.
If one recites it fifteen hundred times every day for six full months,
all sought-after siddhis will be accomplished. Furthermore,
according to another method, after having purified oneself by bathing:
Sitting upon a seat of triradial grass,
recite three hundred and fifty thousand times;
there will be no *siddhi* whatsoever that one does not attain.
Furthermore, one will be free from all diseases of the body and shall certainly not suffer from untimely calamities.
If one recites this mantra ten thousand times before the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
all sought-after virtuous aspirations shall be accomplished.
Furthermore, according to another method, on the eighth or fifteenth day of the waxing moon,
one should bathe with purity and recite [the mantra] eight thousand times;
this will enable one to escape all untimely calamities throughout the world.
All demonic obstacles will be completely extinguished.
Furthermore, if one observes the eight precepts from the first to the fifteenth day of the waxing moon and recites this ten thousand times daily,
one will be able to remain free from all hindrances and difficulties caused by the Vināyakas.
Furthermore, from the first day of the first month until the fifteenth day,
one should purify a maṇḍala before the Buddha and make offerings of incense and flowers.
If one recites this thirty-five thousand times,
one will be able to attain all siddhis and whatever is sought.
Furthermore, at dawn, one should bathe with fragrant water.
If one recites it three thousand five hundred times,
one will be able to cause all people to respect and love them;
whatever matters they seek shall all be obtained according to their wishes.
Furthermore, first recite ten thousand times before the Buddha.
Then, beginning from the first day until the fourteenth day, recite one hundred thousand times.
One will thereby remain far removed from all evil obstacles and difficulties.
Furthermore, if there are sons or daughters of good family who construct a maṇḍala before the Buddha and before the various bodhisattvas such as Avalokiteśvara.
By making offerings of unguents, incense, flowers, and lamps,
and reciting [the mantra] three thousand five hundred times,
one will certainly be reborn beneath the feet of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara upon casting off the body.
Furthermore, if one first constructs one hundred thousand stūpas and recites ten thousand times before each stūpa while making offerings according to the ritual,
all sought-after siddhis will be attained.
Having relinquished his body, he was reborn at will in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Furthermore, he used the mud from anthills to fashion one hundred thousand small stupas,
reciting three thousand five hundred times before each and every stupa.
The siddhis sought will be most supreme and most excellent;
whatever the mind contemplates shall be attained.
Even if that person has previously committed the four grave offenses or the five heinous crimes, [they shall succeed].
By relying on this, there is no failure to attain extinction;
at the end of life, one will be reborn at will in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Furthermore, previously, mud was used to create a maṇḍala before the Buddha.
Burn aloeswood incense.
Separately take fine flowers and cast one at the Buddha’s feet with each recitation.
Do this three times a day for up to seven days.
It can extinguish all karmic offenses that would certainly lead to rebirth in hell,
and one shall further attain all sought-after siddhis;
moreover, it does not depend on whether the day or month is auspicious or unfavorable.
Simply bathe with fragrant water during the middle watch of the night, put on new and clean clothes,
and recite [the mantra] three thousand five hundred times;
all evil dreams will be completely extinguished.
Whatever matters the mind seeks shall all be explained within the dream, each clearly and distinctly, without any error.
Furthermore, construct a maṇḍala before me;
as the Dharma Master Cowhide stated, it should be made the size of a cowhide, either square or circular, measuring two or three cubits. Then, prepare eight lamps of cow butter.
Recite ten thousand times daily for up to one month,
as previously described, without speaking to others.
Once the month has passed, one will be able to read the Mahāyāna sūtras of the Buddha and achieve non-forgetfulness.
Being extremely intelligent,
they still see Avalokiteśvara and constantly hear him preaching the Dharma.
Furthermore, those who wish to behold the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara [should do so].
Recite [the mantra] two hundred and fifty thousand times within a stūpa containing relics.
Then, perform a great offering, light a lamp of cow’s ghee, and sit upon triradial grass (śara-grass).
Recite the mantra throughout the night until midnight.
The Noble One then manifested his body.
Upon seeing him, the practitioner rose from his seat to offer worship and pay homage.
Thereupon, the Bodhisattva preached the Dharma for him.
Having heard the Dharma,
this person shall never be separated from the Noble Ones;
they will attain the non-retrogressive bodhisattva stage and continue until the attainment of Buddhahood.
Furthermore, at the shore of a spring flowing directly toward the sea,
one should gather sand to construct ten million stūpas.

Reciting one hundred thousand [mantras] before each stūpa will cause even grave offenses that would lead to rebirth in hell to be extinguished without remainder, even if they are difficult to eliminate.
Furthermore, one shall see that the noble one passes away and is reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, where they will swiftly attain Buddhahood.
Moreover, for as long as six months, one should construct one hundred stupas every day and daily perform the recitation.
All calamities in that land will be extinguished. Furthermore,
if one constructs ten million stupas and recites [the mantra] ten million times, [the same result shall be attained].
They will immediately see Avalokiteśvara listening to the preaching of the Dharma.
Wherever this person goes, anyone who sees them shall immediately attain liberation from the ocean of all suffering.
Furthermore, he remained silent;
having constructed numerous stupas and recited [the mantra] three hundred and fifty thousand times,
he immediately attained siddhi.
Whatever he spoke was always the sound of the Dharma, never failing to accord with his intention.
Furthermore, every day he constructed three thousand five hundred stupas,
reciting [the mantra] seven times before each and every stupa.
I dedicate this merit to all sentient beings who are undergoing suffering.
With this aspiration, may all karmic actions that would cause one to fall into the evil realms and undergo suffering be entirely extinguished.
In this way, whatever this person sees,
they regard it with the same reverence as a servant;
at the end of life, they will be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
Furthermore, if one performs countless secret recitations within a stūpa for a period of fifteen days and dedicates this merit to all sentient beings,
then whatever great vows that person seeks shall all be fulfilled.
Furthermore, having first received the eight precepts, one may recite [the mantra] one koṭi times without speaking;
thus one attains the siddhi of the dhyāna-bhūmi. There is also another method: to recite before the feet of the Noble One.
One shall attain all siddhis.
Furthermore, constantly arouse a heart of compassion and grind sandalwood to smear upon a circular mandala.
Like a lotus leaf,
recite three thousand five hundred times before each of the altars, up to one hundred thousand times.
Having thus read the Mahāyāna sūtras,
one immediately attains intelligence and wisdom;
whatever one desires to recite, whether much or little, one gains mastery over it.
Furthermore, by reciting three hundred and fifty thousand times before the deity while remaining silent,
one will immediately attain supreme and most excellent intelligence.
Moreover, by remaining silent, one gives rise to great compassion.
Eating barley rice, or eating only vegetables, or begging for food and drink,
one should recite [the mantra] one hundred and fifty thousand times according to the specific syllables;
then whatever wishes the mind seeks shall all be accomplished.
With the sole exception of sexual desire,
if one makes offerings to the Noble One in accordance with the Dharma and recites [the mantra] ten thousand times while holding incense, [the desired result will be attained].
Wherever one goes, all that is seen and heard brings joy.
Furthermore, if one rises early, bathes, puts on new clean clothes, and recites this [mantra] one thousand times,
even when there is suddenly a time of famine and a lack of food, [one shall not suffer].
This person will always be provided with abundance wherever they go.
Furthermore, at midnight or at dawn, one should scoop up water and sprinkle it over the body,
reciting as much or as little as one is able.
One will be freed from all fears.
Furthermore, if one consecrates a tooth-stick one thousand times and then chews it,
one will immediately attain eloquence and cause all people to respect and love one.
Furthermore, having empowered beautiful flowers, one first smells them oneself and then gives them to the person before;
they will all regard them with reverence and accept them as they please.
Furthermore, by being able to sit upright and recite as much as one is capable of,
one will always attain peace and happiness.
Moreover, by sitting upright in one's place of rest and reciting eight thousand times, one shall likewise obtain such benefits.
Whatever one seeks, all such wishes shall be fulfilled,
with the sole exception of carnal desire.
Furthermore, by reciting this eight thousand times, one can protect both oneself and others.
Furthermore, take fresh cow dung that has not yet fallen to the ground,
mix it with water to form mud,
and grind it into a mandala before the Buddha, Dharma, Saṅgha, and the tutelary deity.
Scatter fragrant flowers upon it,
light a lamp of cow’s ghee,
and sit facing east; having recited [the mantra] ten thousand times, [the rite is complete].
He then lay down to sleep upon the trident-grass at that spot,
recounting in full detail everything he sought in his heart without omitting or forgetting a single thing.
Furthermore, on the first day of the waxing moon, as before, he took *gomaya* (cow dung) to construct an altar.
Scatter fragrant flowers upon it,
light three lamps, and recite [the mantra] three thousand five hundred times.
By morning, you will obtain four *kārsāpaṇas*.
Furthermore, within a śarīra stūpa or before a Buddha image,
one should grind sandalwood powder to create four small altars,
place a ghee lamp on each, and recite [the mantra] three thousand five hundred times.
Whosoever follows this shall have all calamities and misfortunes eliminated and utterly extinguished.
Furthermore, one should take *gomaya* (cow dung),
first mix it with water, and smear it upon the ground.
Then, for the sake of the Buddha, Dharma, Sangha, and the tutelary deity,
prepare four small circular altars using white sandalwood scented water.
Scatter flowers upon them and recite [the mantra] ten thousand times daily.
After seven days have passed, one will immediately obtain various garments.
Furthermore, one should make offerings of incense and flowers to the *iṣṭadevatā*,
light four butter lamps, and recite [the mantra] ten thousand times.
The twenty-first day is as described above.
Furthermore, on the bank of a river or spring that flows directly into the sea,
one should place an image of the Honzon facing west.
Anoint the ground with *gomaya* and make offerings of incense and flowers.
Facing east, the practitioner shall recite [the mantra] three hundred and fifty thousand times.
Thereafter, in this land, wind and rain will follow their proper seasons and the five grains will ripen; furthermore, one should recite it ten thousand more times while burning *nemala* flowers.
In this realm, the fierce winds and heavy rains of evil shall cease, and the withered flowers shall be offered.
Furthermore, should a sudden calamity arise in any kingdom,
one should install the Honored One before the city gate according to the ritual method.
By prostrating and making offerings of various incenses, flowers, food, and drink,
calamities will immediately cease.
Furthermore, one may offer the remains of flowers previously presented to the Noble Ones.
If one performs eight thousand empowerments (*adhiṣṭhāna*) over it and places it upon the head of a patient suffering from severe fever,
and further burns it as incense mixed with clarified butter (*ghṛta*) for that patient,
the intense heat will immediately be relieved and the illness cured.
Furthermore, before the image, light a ghee lamp and perform eight thousand recitations of the empowerment.
Taking the smoke from the lamp and applying it to the eyes will be able to eliminate all eye diseases.
Furthermore, if a plague of death should suddenly arise within the kingdom,
one should paint my image at each of the city gates and offer various flowers grown in water.
Then, at midnight, one should take leaves of the *śamī* tree, dip them in clarified butter (*ghṛta*) using *kūṭaja* wood as a ladle, and perform *homa* offerings until the fifteenth day.
All calamities of death shall cease.
Furthermore, if various disasters caused by venomous insects arise,
first perform offerings before the tutelary deity according to the ritual rules.
Go to a fine spring that is free from the defilement of crows and birds.
Let the water reach the navel.
Take one thousand petals of *sumana* flowers and place them on the left side.
Recite the mantra once for each flower and cast it into the spring;
when the flowers are exhausted, all venomous insects and calamities will be extinguished.
Furthermore, if one recites it ten thousand times beginning at midnight, [the same result shall be achieved].
There will certainly be no bad dreams.
Furthermore, at noon,
enter the spring water facing the sea and recite all [mantras] ten thousand times.
Evil dreams will be extinguished.
Furthermore, empower one's palm eight hundred times and rub it upon the body of one suffering from a feverish illness.
If one lies down in a clean place, one will immediately recover.
I shall now explain the method for painting the image:
take a piece of pure cotton cloth that has never been cut.
A young maiden weaver is the most excellent [subject for the painting].
In the center, one should depict the Tathāgata Amitābha,
six *vitasti* in height.
He forms the Dharma-teaching mudrā and sits in the full lotus posture upon a lotus pedestal;
his body is pure golden in color, emitting white flames of light.
To the Buddha’s right, one should paint the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
To the left is painted the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta;
both are entirely golden in color and emit white flames of light.
The right hands of both bodhisattvas each hold a white fly-whisk.
Each holds a lotus flower in the left hand.
Mahāsthāmaprāpta’s body is slightly smaller than that of Avalokiteśvara.
Both have their bodies adorned with various kinds of jewels.
They wear precious necklaces and bracelets;
all are dressed in white garments,
and their hair is tied up at the top, not allowed to hang down.
To the right of the sun, one should paint the noble lady,
the Bodhisattva Pañcarakṣā Bhagavatī, the Mother Avalokiteśvarī clad in white robes; her hair is likewise tied upward,
and she is adorned with a jeweled crown and various precious garments.
Wearing white garments, his celestial robes appear black;
his left hand holds a staff or a noose,
while his right hand grasps a Prajñāpāramitā manuscript.
Below Mahāsthāmaprāpta,
one should depict the practitioner holding a flower crown or a red or blue lotus.
Beholding the venerable countenance of the Buddha:
directly beneath the Buddha’s seat is a lotus pond,
in the center of which a precious lotus is depicted.
On the right side of the lotus is painted the Nanda Dragon King,
and on the left is painted the Upananda Dragon King;
both stand with their upper bodies half-emerged from the water.
Each extended one hand to support the Buddha’s seat upon a lotus flower;
their countenances were joyful, and they adorned their bodies with jewels.
The body is red in color;
on either side of the pond are celestial maidens,
their bodies clad in precious garments.
With both hands holding flowers, they offer them upward to the Tathāgata.
Behind the Buddha, one should paint a wish-fulfilling jewel tree (*cintāmaṇi-vṛkṣa*),
upon which various precious garments and diverse jewels are suspended.
Furthermore, one should depict celestial beings upon the trees, including those providing music, performing dances, and singing birds,
scattering flowers with their hands as rain over the Buddha.
Once the painted image is completed,
place it facing west in a clean location.
Each time one observes the eight precepts, [perform the ritual].
He gave rise to great compassion for all sentient beings,
vigorously aroused the bodhicitta, and made offerings with utmost sincerity.
Before each Buddha image, he personally constructed small stupas and recited the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra.
On either the eighth or the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight,
one should make offerings to the community of monks according to one's means, however great or small;
even if one cannot afford much, one should give at least as little as a single *śu* of parched grain flour.
Before this image, one should make offerings according to the Dharma with various types of unguents, powdered incense, burning incense, food, and drink,
as well as flowers, lamps, banners, canopies, and music; meanwhile,
one should constantly keep Amitābha Buddha in mind.
If one recites its mantra three hundred and fifty thousand times,
one will immediately attain siddhi;
thereafter, all that is brought to mind will be spontaneously accomplished.
I shall now further explain the method for carving an image.
Take a piece of white sandalwood and carve Amitābha Buddha in its center.
To the right is Avalokiteśvara and to the left is Mahāsthāmaprāpta;
each holds a white fly-whisk,
and their robes, necklaces, and other ornaments are all in accordance with the dharma.
Except for ponds and the like,
one should construct a homa hearth before this image.
Within the hearth, first place the five grains and the five precious gems.
Kindle a fire using *aśvattha* wood;
mix together ghee, honey, milk, curd, and various kinds of flowers,
and place them in a vessel made of gold, silver, or copper.
Recite [the mantra] two thousand five hundred times,
then perform the homa ritual.
Begin on the first day of the waxing moon and continue for seven days.
If one performs the homa in this manner three thousand five hundred times each day,
whatever matter one seeks will surely accord with one's original vow and the siddhi will be attained.
Thereafter, one will attain mastery over all dharmas performed at will.
Furthermore, by kindling a fire with *bībhā* wood and performing two thousand five hundred *homa* offerings of non-glutinous rice mixed with the three sweets,
everyone from the king downward will become joyful and compliant.
Furthermore, as described above, if one kindles a fire with *pārasa* wood and performs two thousand five hundred *homa* offerings of non-glutinous rice and curd,
those within the kingdom will hold one in high esteem, obeying whatever one says, and wealth and treasures will be obtained at will.
Furthermore, by performing a homa with the three sweets using *ābalyamṛgaja* wood (*vīratara*), ghee, and sesame oil,
all *śūdras* will be deeply respectful and compliant. Moreover,
by performing a homa with the three sweets using *aśoka* wood (*anoka*) as described above for up to seven days, [the same result is achieved].
The king will act according to one's wishes.

Furthermore, using *rājavṛkṣa*—which means "king-tree" and refers to the *bhallātaka* (soapberry) tree—perform the homa with the three sweets for seven days as previously described, substituting *aśvattha* (holy fig) wood for *nyagrodha* (banyan) wood.
Furthermore, using wood with milky sap as described above,
perform homa with this same wood for twenty-one days;
all serious illnesses will be completely dispelled.
It shall not arise again throughout one's entire life.
Furthermore, using *pāṭala* wood as described above,
one should perform *homa* with the five grains and clarified butter for as long as three months.
When the five grains have ripened in abundance, one should perform [the rite] two thousand five hundred times as described above. Furthermore, using *udumbara* wood as before,
one should perform *homa* three times daily for up to one month, using barley and clarified butter, totaling three thousand five hundred [oblations].
One obtains a cow that yields excellent milk.
Furthermore, as with the *pāṭala* wood mentioned above,
one uses red soybeans boiled to make a soup.

With white non-glutinous rice, clarified butter, and honey, perform *homa* three times a day for three thousand five hundred [times]; one will obtain a treasury of wealth and treasures that remains full and inexhaustible for all uses.
Furthermore, use *khadira* wood as described above.
Perform three thousand five hundred homa offerings with bilva wood for up to seven days;
one will obtain one thousand *suvarṇas*.
Furthermore, perform [homa] with palāśa wood as described above.
Furthermore, perform three thousand five hundred oblations with the three sweets using these same woods.
The person one has in mind will arrive at the appointed time; one should then respectfully make offerings to them.
Also, the udumbara wood is used as described above.
Perform three thousand five hundred *homa* offerings with non-glutinous rice and clarified butter (*sarpis*);
then wealth, treasures, and the five grains will be obtained according to one's wishes without end.
Furthermore, perform [the same] with *pārśa* wood as described above.
Perform three thousand five hundred *homa* offerings using yellow rice, millet, sesame, barley, and clarified butter;
then the king shall obtain whatever he desires.
Furthermore, using the aforementioned milky wood,
perform three thousand five hundred *homa* offerings with non-glutinous rice and clarified butter;
one will immediately attain unimpeded eloquence and become uniquely preeminent among men.
Furthermore, as with the *amala* fruit mentioned above,
perform *homa* offerings using *aśvattha* wood combined with the three sweets for seven days,
reciting the mantra eight thousand times each day.
Upon recollecting [the deity], one arrives immediately, like a servant seeing his master.
Furthermore, the *pārijātaka* tree is as described above;
[one should offer it] with barley and the three sweets.
Perform the homa for three thousand five hundred times, or even for twenty-one days.
Recite as many times as there are people, as previously described.
Furthermore, use the aforementioned wood in the same manner as above.
Using three sweets with non-glutinous rice,
perform *homa* three thousand five hundred times daily for as long as one month;
then the Brahmin will arrive at the mere thought of him and will not fail to carry out whatever he is commanded.
Furthermore, as with the *āpāmārga* wood mentioned above,
one should perform *homa* with sesame seeds and barley mixed with clarified butter for three thousand five hundred times, or for up to twenty-one days.
Having obtained all the precious and honored items from the *kṣatriya* nobles as desired,
one should prepare [an offering] of *gokṣura* and *khadira* wood as described above,
mixed with yellow millet, sesame, and clarified butter (*sarpis*).
Perform three thousand five hundred homa offerings.
For those of the Vaiśya caste, it is as previously described.
Furthermore, the udumbara wood is as mentioned above.
Barley and the three sweets are to be understood according to the aforementioned quantities.
A person of the Śūdra caste is as described before.
Furthermore, the *aśoka* wood is as above.
Using *pārijātaka* wood and the three sweets,
following the aforementioned count up to seven days,
the king will show respect according to his wishes.
Furthermore, as with the *bāla* and *bhallātaka* wood mentioned above,
one should take *pārśa* wood, dip it in the three sweets,
and perform the ritual according to the aforementioned count for up to seven days.
The princes and others followed their recollections and arrived, treating them with great reverence.
Furthermore, the *aśvattha* wood is as described above;
sesame seeds and non-glutinous rice mixed with ghee and curd are to be prepared according to the same standard.
The five grains may be used as one pleases without limit.

Furthermore, the *śamī* wood may be substituted for the *guji* wood as prescribed above; likewise, the *aśvattha* wood may be substituted for the *yehé* (nyagrodha) wood according to the same standard, continuing up until the twenty-first day.
One will be far removed from all accidental calamities and grave illnesses.
Furthermore, as with the *pārijātaka* wood mentioned above,
one may likewise use sesame seeds mixed with clarified butter for up to three months according to the same procedure.
One shall obtain immeasurable quantities of the five grains.
Furthermore, regarding the *pārijāta* wood as described above,
one should combine polished rice, red small beans, a soup of yellow millet and large barley, along with the three sweets.
The date and time are as specified above.
One shall obtain countless and inexhaustible precious jewels.
Furthermore, the *pāṭala* and *kṣa* wood are as described above.
Using *pāraśa* wood and the three sweets,
following the procedure above for up to twenty-one days,
one will obtain clothing as desired, inexhaustibly.
Furthermore, regarding the *bhr̥ṅgarāja* as described above,
one should mix it with incense leaves, non-glutinous rice, and the three sweets,
performing this three times daily for up to one month according to the previous procedure.
One obtains five estates of cultivated fields.

Furthermore, one may substitute *karṇikāra* wood for peonies as described above; by mixing this with *vātana* and *āmalaka* along with clarified butter (*sarpis*), taking it three times daily according to the aforementioned method for up to one month, one will obtain immeasurable *supārṇa*.
Furthermore, using *pāraśa* wood as described above,
combine *gāthāra* wood with honey and curdled milk;
following the procedure above for up to twenty-one days, one will obtain what is called "the horse fit for riding."
Furthermore, as with the *aśvattha* wood mentioned above,
one should combine *palāśa* wood with the two sweets;
three times each day, following the aforementioned quantities, this should be continued for up to one month.
One will obtain the fruit of wealth and nobility.
Furthermore, regarding the *pārijātaka* wood as described above,
one should mix it with the three sweets and *guggulu* incense.
Following the above procedure up to twenty-one days, one will obtain fields and lands.
Furthermore, regarding the *bhallātaka* fruit as described above,
mix white mustard seeds with clarified butter (*ghṛta*).
Performing this three times a day for a total of twenty-one days as described above,
one will ensure that both oneself and one’s disciples remain free from serious illness.
Furthermore, the wood of the *vainayika-kadaka* tree is used as previously stated.
Using *vāśī* incense mixed with clarified butter and honey,
following the aforementioned number of times for a total of seven days,
all evil obstructions and difficulties will be eliminated.
Furthermore, regarding the *pālakīśa* wood as described above:
take the fruit of the *udumbara* tree, mix it with the three sweets,
and follow the aforementioned procedure for three periods each day for one month.
It is known by one hundred and eight names.
Furthermore, the *pārijāta* tree is as described above;
it is combined with lotus seeds and the three sweets.
Three times each day, as prescribed above,
whatever one seeks shall be fulfilled according to one's wishes.
Furthermore, the *śamaya* wood is as described above.
Mixing the seeds of the *pārāsa* fruit with the three sweets,
perform the ritual three times daily as described above for one month;
then all requested wishes will be completely fulfilled.
Furthermore, regarding the *mota* wood as described above,
one should mix pomegranate seeds with the three sweets three times daily,
following the aforementioned procedure for a full month.
One obtains twenty fields and gardens.
Furthermore, as with the *śrīsaṃyāha* wood mentioned above,
one uses the dung of a calf.
